21476.title_note: bodysuite 拼写错纠正；crossover→Criss-Cross；lace tassels 参数回填；双色属实
21476.desc:
Tassels on a bodysuit are movement you can hear: they do nothing statically and everything the moment the wearer moves. This bodysuit mounts its lace trim as fringe at the edges, over a criss-cross front in high-stretch fabric, so the piece has two speeds — a fitted one-piece at rest, and a lot of small swinging details in motion.

The criss-cross front is the fit mechanism as much as the look: the straps cross at the bust and can be arranged rather than fastened, which lets one size cover a real range. The base fabric is polyester with serious recovery, which matters in a bodysuit — it has to snap back from every wear.

Black and gray versions read almost like different garments: the black hides the sheer panels until the light hits, the gray announces them quietly. Both take the same cold wash.

Quick specs:

  • Fabric: High-stretch polyester with lace trim
  • Style: Criss-cross bodysuit with tassel trim
  • Colors: Black, gray
  • Fit: One size, recommended 85–130 lbs (39–59 kg)

Two speeds, one bodysuit.
21476.short: Criss-cross bodysuit in high-stretch polyester with swinging tassel lace trim, black or gray, one size for 85–130 lbs weight range.
21476.tkd_desc: High-stretch criss-cross bodysuit with swinging tassel lace trim, black or gray, one size for 85-130 lbs. Shop at RoseToys.

21493.new_name: Polka-Dot Mesh Lingerie Set with Straps
21493.title_note: printing dot→Polka-Dot；ribbon binding→Straps；sex set 堆词剥；五码 S-XXL 属实
21493.desc:
Polka dots are the friendliest pattern in sheer fabric: they give the eye somewhere to rest and give the mesh a scale it otherwise lacks. This set prints its dots across a soft mesh, then runs adjustable strapping over the top — across the bust and at the waist — so the pattern and the hardware share the design without competing.

The set is a bra-and-bottom pairing with real adjustability: the straps cinch by slider, which is what lets a single style serve five sizes from S to XXL. The mesh has enough stretch to sit smooth under the strapping rather than puckering around it, and the seam work is flat where it matters.

Seamless construction means no wires and no hooks to negotiate with — the whole set works on stretch and adjustment, which is the entire reason it can fit such a wide range of bodies.

The rundown:

  • Fabric: Polka-dot stretch mesh
  • Pieces: Strap bra and matching bottom
  • Sizes: S, M, L, XL, XXL

Friendly pattern, serious hardware, five sizes of fit.
21493.short: Polka-dot mesh lingerie set with adjustable strapping across bust and waist, seamless and wireless, five sizes from S to XXL.

21542.desc:
Leaf lace is the classic of the teddy genre for a reason: the motif scales from delicate at the strap to dense at the cup, so one fabric reads as several textures across a single piece. This bodysuit uses it front and back — a deep-V neckline filled with the leaf pattern, and a backless rear where the lace thins to its sheerest.

The straps cross at the back, which does double duty as the design and the adjustability: criss-crossing changes both the look and the fit, and the slider hardware lets the wearer set both once. The cut runs short through the torso by design — a mini teddy, not a bodystocking.

Five sizes from S to XXL, which in lace this detailed is the difference between the pattern sitting flat and it stretching into something it is not. Pairing advice from the design itself: a satin robe over the top turns it into pajamas without changing anything underneath.

What you are getting:

  • Fabric: Leaf-pattern stretch lace with polyester
  • Style: Deep-V mini teddy bodysuit
  • Key details: Backless, adjustable criss-cross straps
  • Sizes: S, M, L, XL, XXL

One classic motif, worn as a single garment.
21542.short: Deep-V mini teddy in leaf-pattern stretch lace, backless with adjustable criss-cross straps, in five honest sizes from S to XXL.

A maxi dress in lingerie is a power move: the length reads as elegance, the sheer reads as intent, and the combination does work that shorter cuts cannot. This one runs full length in polyester with a deep-V neckline and a high slit at the leg — the classic trio — then adds chain detailing as the signature, because three familiar elements plus one metallic one is how a look gets remembered.

The chains sit as trim rather than structure, so they move with the fabric instead of holding it. The set beneath includes a matching T-back panty, which the maxi length keeps discreet until the slit decides otherwise.

Sizing runs by weight bands in pounds: M for 105–120 lbs, L for 120–140 lbs, and XL for 140–155 lbs. In a floor-length piece the band matters — the slit lands where it lands, and the fit determines whether that is exactly right.

  • Key details: Deep-V neckline, high slit, chain accents

Buying a jumpsuit with its own skirt is a two-look decision made in one purchase: the jumpsuit alone is the plain statement, and the skirt over it turns the same piece into a layered outfit with a different silhouette. This chiffon set sells exactly that choice — open-work jumpsuit, plus a matching short skirt that can be worn or left.

The jumpsuit is the base: chiffon in an open-work pattern, tied at the front rather than fastened, with the tie doing the fitting and the adjusting. The skirt is deliberately simple — a plain short overlay in the same fabric, sized to move independently of what is under it.

Black and gray versions of both pieces. One size covers the 40–60 kg band; chiffon is doing the draping, so the band has more slack than a fitted cut would.

  • Pieces: Tie-up jumpsuit, matching short skirt (skirt optional in wear)

The secret-agent reference in lingerie is really about the strapping: harness lines across an otherwise plain bodysuit, the way film costume designers signal tactical without issuing a weapon. This jumpsuit builds the look in polyester — a fitted base with wide strapping at the shoulders and torso — and includes the decorative hardware that sells the character.

The base layer is a real garment, not just a mount for the straps: fitted through the body, with a 70–120 cm chest range and 60–90 cm waist range under the single size, so the strapping sits against fabric rather than pinching skin. The sets come in black or gray — one for night work, one for the office-party version of it.

As a costume it needs no explanation; as lingerie it needs none either. The strapping is the entire design statement, and it is load-bearing.

A bra-and-panty set is judged by its lace first and everything else second, because at two small pieces the fabric is most of what there is. This set spends well: a criss-cross floral lace with a two-part back closure on the bra — an actual closure, not just stretch — and a matching panty cut to the same pattern.

One size covers the standard band, with the lace doing the absorbing. There are no wires and no hooks beyond the back closure — the set is built to be worn through an evening and then through the night, in that order or the other one.

This piece keeps the pairing honest — a chiffon-and-lace costume piece with a G-string bottom, all in black, sized for the standard band.

The construction is one costume piece plus the G-string, which is the entire inventory: no strapping to arrange, no hardware to hear, nothing but the two pieces and their combined effect. The lace does the design work at the bust and hem; the chiffon keeps the body of it light.

Worn as sleepwear it is nearly weightless; worn as lingerie it is the genre's default setting. The G-String is matched to the lace rather than contrasted against it — a small detail that separates sets designed together from sets assembled.
